es: Clasificar enunciados de un informe como hecho, inferencia u opinión según su formulación y señalar la pista lingüística.

teaching.en: It is a fact that 62 percent of the students sleep less than eight hours, and the report names its source so that readers can check the figure.
teaching.es: Es un hecho que el 62 % de los estudiantes duerme menos de ocho horas, y el informe nombra su fuente para que los lectores puedan comprobar la cifra.
teaching.explanationEs: Fact: algo que se puede comprobar, con cifras o fuente. En inglés es obligatorio el sujeto it en It is a fact that…
segments: It is a fact that 62 percent of the students sleep less than eight
hours, and the report names its source so that readers can check the figure.
teaching.audioText: It is a fact that 62 percent of the students sleep less than eight hours, and the report names its source so that readers can check the figure.

teaching.en: We can assume that the school cut homework, but that is an inference, not a fact, and we would need the school's records to confirm it.
teaching.es: Podemos suponer que el colegio redujo las tareas, pero eso es una inferencia, no un hecho, y necesitaríamos los registros del colegio para confirmarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Una inferencia se deduce de los hechos; assume y suggest son pistas de que no está comprobada.
segments: We can assume that the school cut homework, but that is an inference,
not a fact, and we would need the school's records to confirm it.
teaching.audioText: We can assume that the school cut homework, but that is an inference, not a fact, and we would need the school's records to confirm it.

teaching.en: Whether homework should be shorter is a matter of opinion, and unfortunately nobody asked the students what they think about it.
teaching.es: Si las tareas deberían ser más cortas es cuestión de opinión, y por desgracia nadie preguntó a los estudiantes qué piensan al respecto.
teaching.explanationEs: A matter of opinion: no se puede comprobar. In my opinion, should y unfortunately son pistas de opinión: valoran en lugar de comprobar.
segments: Whether homework should be shorter is a matter of opinion, and
unfortunately nobody asked the students what they think about it.
teaching.audioText: Whether homework should be shorter is a matter of opinion, and unfortunately nobody asked the students what they think about it.

teaching.en: According to the school nurse, the source of the figure is a national survey, which is more reliable than second-hand stories from the corridor.
teaching.es: Según la enfermera del colegio, la fuente de la cifra es una encuesta nacional, que es más fiable que las historias de segunda mano del pasillo.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + persona o documento atribuye el dato; second-hand describe información que llega a través de otros. No se dice «according to me».
segments: According to the school nurse, the source of the figure is a
national survey, which is more reliable than second-hand stories from the corridor.
teaching.audioText: According to the school nurse, the source of the figure is a national survey, which is more reliable than second-hand stories from the corridor.

teaching.en: Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but that is speculation until someone tests it, so the certainty of the statement is low.
teaching.es: Presumiblemente, el uso de pantallas por la noche explica la caída, pero eso es especulación hasta que alguien lo compruebe, así que la certeza de la afirmación es baja.
teaching.explanationEs: Presumably marca una inferencia: probable, no comprobada; speculation es una idea sin pruebas.
segments: Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but that is speculation until
someone tests it, so the certainty of the statement is low.
teaching.audioText: Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but that is speculation until someone tests it, so the certainty of the statement is low.

teaching.en: Reportedly, the school has cut homework by a third, although I cannot confirm it, and the evidence so far is only anecdotal and rather subjective.
teaching.es: Según se dice, el colegio ha reducido las tareas en un tercio, aunque no puedo confirmarlo, y las pruebas hasta ahora son solo anecdóticas y bastante subjetivas.
teaching.explanationEs: Reportedly atribuye la información a otros sin confirmarla; anecdotal y subjective describen pruebas basadas en casos sueltos o en impresiones personales.
segments: Reportedly, the school has cut homework by a third, although I cannot confirm
it, and the evidence so far is only anecdotal and rather subjective.
teaching.audioText: Reportedly, the school has cut homework by a third, although I cannot confirm it, and the evidence so far is only anecdotal and rather subjective.

prompt.es: Lee el extracto y elige cómo clasificar «Presumably, late screen use explains the drop».

choices.text: Fact: the nurse states it, so it has been checked and confirmed.
Opinion: unfortunately shows that the writer is unhappy about it.
Inference: presumably marks a likely explanation that has not been tested.

feedback.es: Presumably presenta la explicación como probable pero sin comprobar: es una inferencia, no un hecho ni una opinión.

hint.es: Busca la palabra que dice que algo es probable pero no está comprobado.

origin.text: Extract from the report: 'According to the school nurse, 62 percent of students sleep fewer than eight hours. Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but no one has tested this idea. Unfortunately, the school has done nothing about it so far.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Podemos suponer que redujeron las tareas, pero nadie lo ha probado.»

feedback.es: Assume (o presume) introduce una suposición; en un informe indica una inferencia que aún no está comprobada.

hint.es: Es el verbo que introduce algo que damos por probable, sin pruebas.

origin.text: The report says that homework is lighter this year. We can ___ that the school cut it, but nobody has proved this yet. That is an inference, not a fact.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Según la enfermera, la fuente de la cifra es una encuesta nacional.»

answer.text: According to the nurse the source of the figure is a national survey

feedback.es: According to + persona atribuye el dato y source permite comprobarlo: es la estructura típica de un hecho.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula que atribuye el dato a una persona.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué frase de la lectura es una opinión y por qué.

choices.text: That the timetable is an excellent improvement, because that word expresses a personal view.
That seventy percent prefer the new timetable, because the figure has no named source.
That attendance will rise, because the writer is completely sure about the result.

feedback.es: La profesora señala que excellent es una valoración personal: por eso esa frase es una opinión. La cifra tiene fuente y la subida de asistencia es una inferencia.

origin.audio: A teacher is reading a school report aloud and commenting on it. The report says that seventy percent of students prefer the new timetable. That is a fact, she says, because the figure comes from a named survey. Then it says that the new timetable is an excellent improvement. That, she explains, is an opinion, and the word excellent gives it away. Finally, the report says that presumably attendance will rise. That is an inference, because nobody has checked it yet.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada pista lingüística con el tipo de enunciado.

feedback.es: Cada pista apunta a un tipo: fuente y cifra, probabilidad, valoración o información atribuida a otros.

prompt.es: Elige cómo clasificar el titular según el estudio que cita el artículo.

choices.text: A plain fact: the study has measured the forty minutes of lost sleep.
An overstated inference: the study shows a difference, not a reason.
Simply an opinion, because the headline contains no figure at all.

feedback.es: El estudio mide una diferencia de 40 minutos, pero el titular la presenta como motivo: es una inferencia exagerada.

origin.text: Headline: 'Phones are the reason why teenagers sleep badly.' Below it, the article quotes one study: teenagers who use their phones at night sleep forty minutes less, on average, than those who do not.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hará la periodista con la frase sobre la cantina.

choices.text: Print it as a fact, since the school office said so.
Delete it, because it is only the opinion of the parents.
Ask the school for evidence before she prints it.

feedback.es: La periodista subraya la frase, la considera una inferencia y no la publicará hasta que el colegio aporte pruebas.

origin.audio: A journalist is checking a school press release before publishing it. The release says that attendance has reached ninety-five percent, according to the school office. That is a fact that can be checked, she notes, and she will confirm it with the office. It then says that the new canteen is the reason for the improvement. She underlines that statement: it is an inference at best, because the release gives no evidence, and she will not print it until the school provides some. Finally, the release says that all the parents are happy. She crosses that out, since nobody has asked them: in her view it is only a guess presented as a fact.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige por qué tacha la frase sobre los padres.

choices.text: Because nobody asked the parents, so it is a guess.
Because the school office has already denied it publicly.
Because it is a fact, but one that the school office has not confirmed.

feedback.es: Nadie ha preguntado a los padres: la frase es una suposición que el comunicado presenta como si fuera un hecho.

origin.audio: A journalist is checking a school press release before publishing it. The release says that attendance has reached ninety-five percent, according to the school office. That is a fact that can be checked, she notes, and she will confirm it with the office. It then says that the new canteen is the reason for the improvement. She underlines that statement: it is an inference at best, because the release gives no evidence, and she will not print it until the school provides some. Finally, the release says that all the parents are happy. She crosses that out, since nobody has asked them: in her view it is only a guess presented as a fact.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nadie ha comprobado esta idea, así que es pura especulación y no un hecho.»

feedback.es: Speculation es una idea sin pruebas; presentarla como un hecho confunde al lector.

origin.text: Nobody has tested this idea, so it is nothing more than ___ and should not be presented as a fact. A careful writer would label it as a guess.

prompt.es: Elige la opción que clasifica bien las tres frases del boletín.

choices.text: A is an inference, B is a fact, C is an opinion.
A is a fact, B is an opinion, C is an inference.
A is an opinion, B is an inference, C is a fact.

feedback.es: A lleva cifra y fuente (hecho); B usa obviously y best (opinión); C usa presumably (inferencia).

origin.text: Statements from a town newsletter. A: 'The library has added 4,000 new members since January, according to the council.' B: 'The library is obviously the best place in town.' C: 'Presumably, the new café inside explains the rise.'

prompt.es: Lee la columna y elige qué da a entender el autor sobre la decisión del consejo.

choices.text: That the decision is understandable, since a parent says that fewer children use the pool.
That the decision is only a rumour with no official record at all.
That the decision was taken without checking the facts, in his view.

feedback.es: Unfortunately y presumably muestran su opinión; además contrapone la versión de un padre a las cifras oficiales, que muestran una subida.

origin.text: Column: 'Unfortunately, the council has reportedly decided to close the pool. Presumably, nobody checked how many children use it. One parent said that attendance had fallen, although the council's own figures, published in March, show a rise.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo describe la amiga la frase sobre el laboratorio nuevo.

choices.text: As information from others that the writer has not confirmed.
As a fact that the writer has checked with the school.
As a personal opinion that the writer has made up.

feedback.es: Reportedly atribuye la noticia a otros, y el autor admite que no la ha confirmado.

origin.audio: Two friends are discussing an article. One says that it claims the school is the best in the region. The other says that this is only an opinion, because it does not say where the figures come from. She adds that the article also says, reportedly, that the school will open a new lab, but the writer admits that he has not confirmed it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una afirmación sin fuente identificada es difícil de comprobar.»

feedback.es: Sin una fuente identificada, un dato no se puede verificar, por llamativo que sea.

origin.text: A claim without a named ___ is hard to check, so careful readers treat it with care. Even a striking number means little if nobody can say where it comes from.
